scope: Storage failures, bounded waits, and unknown outcomes: storage_failed reasons, a bounded wait for a document's turn, request_in_progress for a repeated request_id answered without waiting for other locks, replies of finished requests returned before the turn, and the web client's handling of saves, creates, and copies whose reply was lost
environment: Linux 6.6 (WSL2), Rust 1.95.0, Node 22.22.2; browser checks with Chromium 141.0.7390.37 (Playwright build v1194) via playwright-core 1.56.1
design: Writes that commit a document or touch its draft (and creates) first mark their request_id as running in a small table whose lock is never held across storage I/O or another lock; a repeated request_id still running is answered request_in_progress from there. Then a completed request with that ID is looked up, and only then does the request wait, at most 3 s, for the document's turn. This replaces an earlier attempt (#18) whose replay and in-progress checks took the session table lock first, which a copy holds during its storage I/O.

checks.cargo_test: 81 tests pass (domain 20, application 35, providers 17, api 9). New: the turn table's four unit tests; storage_failures_say_whether_retrying_can_help, requests_queued_behind_a_stalled_save_are_answered_busy_without_changes, a_save_whose_reply_was_lost_is_reported_by_asking_again, a_finished_request_asked_about_again_is_answered_while_another_holds_the_turn, a_copy_asked_about_while_it_writes_is_answered_at_once, a_request_id_kept_per_process_is_in_progress_for_every_document_while_it_runs (application); a_write_refused_by_permissions_is_denied_and_changes_nothing, a_read_refused_by_permissions_is_not_reported_as_read_only_storage (providers). The lost-reply tests also check that storage was not written again.
checks.contract_smoke: Passes with real API and CLI processes. The API's save pauses 15 s inside its save lock (CHEMIFREE_TEST_COMMIT_DELAY_MS, debug builds only), detected with a non-blocking flock probe rather than a sleep. Meanwhile: the same request_id is answered 409 request_in_progress at once; a queued save, autosave, and save-as are answered 503 storage_failed busy within 8.5 s; a CLI save of the same document gives up after the 5 s lock wait with reason busy; nothing is committed, copied, or drafted. Afterwards the same request_id returns the committed reply at once and the file is not written again (unchanged mtime). A read-only documents/ gives reason read_only with the file unchanged; a save blocked by a directory in place of the file gives reason io.
checks.browser_smoke: Passes with CHEMIFREE_SMOKE_NO_SKIPS=1 and FORCE_COLOR=1 (results in editor-browser-smoke.json). New steps: read_only_storage_is_named, busy_document_is_named_and_retried, late_save_reply_is_confirmed_not_failed (a reply held 11 s past the page's deadline: asked again once with the same request ID, shown as Saved, committed once), unconfirmed_save_is_checked_not_repeated (two replies dropped: 'Save not confirmed', then Check again confirms the same save; three requests, one ID), and copy_in_progress_keeps_its_request_id (no reply, then request_in_progress, then the copy: three requests, one ID, one copy).
checks.typescript: npm run lint and npm run typecheck pass.
checks.web_client: npm run test:client passes 13 cases: the web client module runs under Node's type stripping against a scripted service. A create polled while another request finds the service restarted, a copy retried after that, and a save checked after that are not resent to the new process (create_unconfirmed, copy_unconfirmed, service_restarted); a create in progress is asked about with one request ID; a first attempt refused by an already restarted service is sent again; a lost save reply is asked about with the same ID; a proxy's 502 without a v1 body counts as no reply (a create is not repeated after a restart, a save is asked about again); a failed session request does not erase where an unknown create was sent; a create or copy answered after being asked about again is read again and shown as it is now (a copy keeps what became of its source); a copy with an empty title and one without a title are different requests; a replayed create whose re-read fails keeps its request ID, so trying again does not create another.

limits: Waits are bounded; storage I/O is not. Creates, autosaves, closes, recoveries, draft discards, and copies do their I/O while holding the process's session table, so a stalled disk delays other requests of the process. Only the in-progress answer for a repeated request_id does not wait for it.

A lost reply is answered from the replay window (the latest 64 successful mutations of an open document; per process for creates and closes). Asked about later, a request runs again, and a save whose revision moved on gets revision_conflict.
The turn wait (3 s) and the lock wait (5 s) are per process.
Read-only storage is reported, but there is no read-only mode for opening documents or saving them elsewhere.
Steps that change directory permissions are skipped when running as root; CI forbids skipped browser steps.

The recover-as-copy request is keyed by document and title, not by draft, so within one process recovering two different drafts of the same document as copies (possible only with two processes on one data directory) can replay the first copy.
